Definition: of Hebrew origin (H5804); Gazah (i.e. Azzah), a place in Palestine:--Gaza.
BiblicalUsage: Gaza is the Philistine city on the way south from Jerusalem, named once in the New Testament in Acts 8:26. The angel of the Lord spoke to Philip, saying, Arise, and go toward the south unto the way that goes down from Jerusalem unto Gaza, which is desert. Philip went, and on that desert road he met the Ethiopian and preached Christ to him.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the road to Gaza is the road of obedience. Philip left a revival in Samaria for a desert road because an angel told him to, and I hold that the greatest fruit often grows on the road we would not have chosen.
